verdict: Texas Pacific Land set records with revenue up 35% to $273.4M and net income of $167.4M, as oil and gas royalties surged 54% on higher prices and Permian drilling.

kpis.label: Oil & gas royalties
kpis.note: A record, +54% YoY on higher prices and production

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: A record (non-GAAP, as the company defines it)

segments.name: Land and Resource Management
segments.note: Royalties and rent from TPL's Permian Basin land: $167.3M of oil and gas royalties, $34.2M of easements and surface income, and $0.1M of land sales. Segment net income was $133.8M.

segments.name: Water Services and Operations
segments.note: Water for oilfield use: $28.4M of water sales and $41.4M of produced-water royalties, plus $2.0M of easements. Segment net income was $33.6M.

opex.name: Salaries & related expenses
opex.note: Pay for the people who manage the land, royalty interests and water business.

opex.name: Water service-related expenses
opex.note: Running the water sourcing, treatment and disposal operations.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — offices, legal and admin. Up from $5.6M a year ago.

opex.name: Depreciation, depletion & amortization
opex.note: The cost of water assets and royalty interests wearing out or being used up over time.

opex.name: Ad valorem & other taxes
opex.note: Property-type taxes on the land and assets — separate from income tax.

otherDetail: Other income of $2.6M, net: $3.6M of other income, net, less $1.0M of interest expense.
footerNote: TPL reports in thousands; figures are shown in $M with decimals so the lines add up exactly. TPL has no separate cost-of-revenue line — all of its costs are operating expenses, so gross profit equals revenue in the flow.

takeaways.title: Royalties set a record
takeaways.text: Oil and gas royalty revenue hit a record $167.3M, up 54% from a year ago. TPL's share of production was a record 42.3 thousand barrels of oil equivalent a day, and realized oil prices averaged $83.57 a barrel.

takeaways.title: Best quarter in company history
takeaways.text: Revenue, net income and free cash flow all set records. Easement and surface income more than doubled to $36.2M as operators built more pipelines and infrastructure across TPL's land.

takeaways.title: The water segment cooled
takeaways.text: Water Services revenue fell 11% to $71.8M: water sales dropped 36% even as produced-water royalty volumes hit a record 5,541 thousand barrels a day and produced-water royalties rose 28% to $41.4M.
